question: A refactor touches 60 files. A single reviewer instance given the entire diff at once produces contradictory findings between files. What change to the review architecture best addresses this?
options: A) Split the review into per-file passes for local issues, plus an integration pass for cross-file consistency
B) Run the same single reviewer instance twice over the full diff, and keep only findings that appear in both runs
C) Ask the generator to make smaller, sequential commits, and review only the most recent commit in full each time
D) Give the single reviewer instance a much larger context window so it can hold the whole diff in memory during one pass
correct_answers: A) Split the review into per-file passes for local issues, plus an integration pass for cross-file consistency
explanations: Correct. Splitting into per-file local passes plus a separate cross-file integration pass avoids the attention dilution and contradictory findings that come from reviewing everything in one undifferentiated pass.
Incorrect. Running the same overloaded single pass twice does not fix attention dilution; it just repeats the same structural problem.
Incorrect. Reviewing only the latest commit in isolation loses the cross-file view needed to catch integration issues across the full 60-file change.
Incorrect. A larger context window doesn't resolve attention dilution across unrelated files or eliminate contradictory findings between them.
